statement.text:
Any set of all subgroups of the same given order of a finite group G that
contains at least one non-normal subgroup is called an IEn̄ -system of G. A positive
integer k is called a soluble (non-soluble; simple; composite; absolutely simple)
group-theoretic number if every finite group having exactly k IEn̄ -systems is soluble
(respectively, if there is at least one non-soluble finite group having k IEn̄ -systems;
if there is at least one simple finite group having k IEn̄ -systems; if there are no
simple finite groups having k IEn̄ -systems; if there is at least one simple finite group
having k IEn̄ -systems and there are no non-soluble non-simple finite groups having
k IEn̄ -systems).
    Are the sets of all soluble and of all absolutely simple group-theoretic numbers
finite or infinite? Do there exist composite, but not soluble group-theoretic numbers?
                                                                             P. I. Trofimov
